title: Microsoft Teams: emoji shortcuts with autocomplete on iOS and Android
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout, default state and existing custom emoji controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. One minor clarification is needed in the impact rationale: the suggestion menu requires a colon followed by at least two characters.

claims.quote: Teams brings desktop-style emoji shortcuts to mobile (iOS and Android)

claims.claim: The desktop client already has the style of emoji shortcuts being introduced on mobile.
claims.quote: We are bringing desktop-style emoji shortcuts to Microsoft Teams on iOS and Android.

claims.claim: The tenant custom emoji UI is Teams admin center > Messaging Settings > Custom emojis > use custom emojis.
claims.quote: In the Teams Admin Center controls, go to Messaging Settings section and toggle the use custom emojis option, found under the Custom emojis section, on or off.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell command Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -CustomEmojis $false disables custom emojis.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -CustomEmojis $False
The command shown in example 1 disables custom emojis within Teams.

claims.where: controls[1].governs, scope and note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The CustomEmojis tenant setting enables or disables use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant.
claims.quote: This setting enables/disables the use of custom emojis and reactions across the whole tenant.

claims.claim: Custom emojis are on by default.
claims.quote: Turn the feature on/off for the whole tenant via the Messaging Settings page (on by default).

claims.claim: The upload setting is at Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Edit > Upload custom emojis.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Messaging policies.
Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.
Upload custom emojis - Set which users can create custom emojis.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -CreateCustomEmojis $false disables creation for users of that messaging policy.
claims.quote:
[-CreateCustomEmojis <Boolean>]
This setting enables the creation of custom emojis and reactions within an organization for the specified policy users.
Identity for the teams messaging policy you're modifying.
